territorial_scope.description: Reaches foreign entities in any foreign country that are owned 50 percent or more by parties on the Entity List, MEU List or designated SDN list.

evidence.quote: These requirements apply to all foreign countries regardless of under which destination the listed entity or entity’s owners are listed.

summary.short: Interim final rule extending Export Administration Regulations end-user license requirements to foreign entities at least 50 percent owned by Entity List, Military End-User List or designated SDN parties. Effective 29 September 2025, it applies to exporters, reexporters and transferors dealing with those affiliates.
summary.long: Interim final rule by the Bureau of Industry and Security amending parts 732, 734, 736, 744 and 748 of the Export Administration Regulations, effective 29 September 2025. It replaces the prior 'legally distinct' standard with a 50 percent ownership rule (the Affiliates rule): foreign entities owned 50 percent or more, directly or indirectly and in aggregate, by Entity List, MEU List or SDN parties are subject to the same license requirements as those parties, and the most restrictive owner's requirements apply. Where an exporter cannot determine the ownership percentage, it must resolve new Red Flag 29, obtain a license or identify a license exception before proceeding. Further provisions cover license application content (supplement no. 2 to part 748, marking 'Affiliates rule'), requests by affiliates to modify owners' listings (sections 744.16(e) and 744.21(b)(2)), and supplement no. 8 guidelines. A temporary general license (General Order No. 7) authorizes certain transactions involving non-listed affiliates; the preamble summary gives its expiry as November 28, 2025, while the regulatory text says December 1, 2025. A savings clause covers shipments en route on 29 September 2025 until 29 October 2025. The End-User Review Committee may grant case-by-case exceptions.

enforcement.note: The text states that exporters, reexporters and transferors can be held liable on a strict liability basis and that knowledge is considered in penalty calculations for EAR violations. It does not describe any sanction regime, its authority, type, maximum penalty or cure period, and it cites no penalty provision (only ECRA 50 U.S.C. 4801-4852 as legal basis).
